english: Dawn, daughter of Sky, grow light!

plan.english: Dawn, daughter of Sky, grow light!

notes: Ved. uṣo ví ucha duhitar divaḥ 'Dawn, shine forth, daughter of Heaven' (RV 1.48.1), the vocative of the title; Greek has the vocative Διὸς θύγατερ (to Aphrodite, Il. 5.348) and of Eos only δῖα < *diw-yā 'of Zeus' (Od. 9.151); West reconstructs pre-Homeric *Diwós tʰugátēr of Dawn. Interpolated: the verb, the -sḱé- present of *h₂wes- 'become light' (Ved. ucchati; Lith. aušta 'it dawns' is the same root but not in a cited passage). Lith. Diẽvo is *deywós (Diẽvas 'god'), not *dyḗws: the Baltic ref supports dʰugh₂tḗr only (dukrýtė, a diminutive of duktė̃), not diwés. RV 1.48.1, Il. 5.348 and Od. 9.151 checked in the local corpora; Rhesa is not in local corpora. The builder's reflex table has no key for Ved. duhitár- or Gk ἠώς, so secure_checks undercount those two.

Ved. úṣo ... ví bhāhi 'Dawn, shine forth' (RV 3.61.2) and Homeric φάε ... Ἠώς 'Dawn shone' (Od. 14.502; φάω from *bʰeh₂-), both checked locally. The Greek is a 3rd-person past, the Vedic an imperative: the mood follows the Vedic. Ved. ví 'forth' has no lexeme. Revised from 'Dawn, immortal one, shine!': Ved. ámartyā (3.61.2) is *-t-yo-, not *n̥mr̥tós, amŕ̥tā stands in another hymn (1.113.13), and Bacchylides' ἄμβροτος is not in a local corpus, so 'immortal' is dropped (it also came out as the engine's feminine eh₂-stem vocative ń̥mr̥teh₂, identical to the nominative, an engine issue not fixable in a plan).

Ved. yukṣvá ... áśvān ... uṣaḥ 'yoke the (red) horses, Dawn' (RV 1.92.15); in the Odyssey Athena holds back Dawn and does not let her yoke (ζεύγνυσθ’) her swift-footed horses (Od. 23.244–246); both checked locally. Revised to the middle, which both branches have (Ved. yukṣvá, s-aorist middle imperative; Gk ζεύγνυσθαι, nasal-present middle): the s-aorist middle imperative follows the Vedic. The stems differ (Vedic s-aorist, Greek -νυ- present), so *yewg- is shared at root level as to formation, and the Greek is negated narrative, not a command. Ved. aruṇā́n 'red' and Gk ὠκύποδας 'swift-footed' differ and are left out.

Dawn rises 'to bring light' (Il. 11.1–2 ἠὼς ... ὄρνυθ’ ἵν’ ... φόως φέροι) and the Vedic Dawns are jyótir bhárantīḥ 'bringing light' (RV 10.35.5, one pāda); both checked locally. *bʰer- and the Dawn are shared; the object follows Gk φόως (*bʰéh₂-os; Ved. jyótis- is another word): interpolated. The Vedic participle and the Greek optative are rendered as a present. Revised: 'to mortals' had been stitched on from another hymn (RV 6.65.3 mártyāya; Ved. mártya- is *mr̥t-yo-, Gk βροτοῖσι *mr̥tó-) and is dropped.

Vedic Dawn 'has been seen' (uṣā́ adarśi, RV 7.77.3; práty adr̥śran, 7.78.3) and is darśatā́ 'a sight to behold'; Hesiod's Dawn is πολυδερκής 'much-seeing' (Th. 451, cited from West 2007 ch. 5), the same root *derḱ-. The Vedic aorist passive is rendered with the middle aorist. Root-level only: Hesiod has the root in a compound with the opposite diathesis ('much-seeing' against Vedic 'was seen'), and West 2007 ch. 5 presents only a root association. RV 7.77.3 and 7.78.3 checked locally; Hesiod is not in local corpora.

Ved. urviyā́ ví bhāti 'she shines out widely' (RV 1.92.9; 6.64.2, of Uṣas) has the elements of the Greek name Εὐρυφάεσσα (εὐρυ- + φα-, Hymn. Hom. 31.2), which Campanile derives from a formula *'broad-shining Dawn' (West 2007 ch. 5). Ved. urviyā́ is an instrumental of urú- used as an adverb: rendered as the instrumental neuter of h₁wérHus. In the hymn Euryphaessa has become Dawn's mother (Eos is named at 31.6), so h₂éwsōs as the one who shines widely is Vedic only and is not counted as secure. Εὐρυφάεσσα is a proper name, so the Greek supports the line only as a name and at root level; the wording rests on Vedic urviyā́ ... bhāti (RV 1.92.9, 6.64.2, both checked). The Homeric Hymn is not in local corpora.

path: erratum:DCS svar 'sun' joined to the verb √svar- 'sound'

notes: West 2007 ch. 5: 'the Sun, like Dyaus/Zeus, has the epithet great ... the Vedic and Greek adjectives are cognate' (RV 3.2.7 súvar mahát, with the neuter sun word like PIE *sóh₂wl̥; RV 2.23.2 Sū́riyo ... mahó, whose construal is uncertain, support; Hes. Th. 19 and 371 Ἠέλιόν τε μέγαν). Copula removed: the daughters have an attributive phrase at RV 3.2.7 (svàr mahát, object of ā́ ... apr̥ṇat) and Hes. Th. 19 (Ἠέλιόν τε μέγαν, in a catalogue of gods), not a predication, so the line is the noun phrase. Revised: 'up goes' came from RV 7.63.2, where mahā́n goes with ketúḥ 'banner', not with the Sun; dropped. RV 3.2.7 and 2.23.2 checked locally (VedaWeb); Hes. Th. 19 checked in GLAUx (0020-001: Ἠέλιόν τε μέγαν, acc. sg., tagged OBJ_CO in the accusative catalogue of gods), so Hesiod is local after all (r4). Case: accusative, as in both parallels (r4: the np had defaulted to NOM): Hes. Th. 19 is accusative, and RV 3.2.7 svàr mahát (VedaWeb NOM/ACC, neuter) is the object of ā́ … apr̥ṇat. The neuter *sóh₂wl̥ has nominative = accusative, so the printed form does not change. Formation (r4): Ved. mahát is the nt-stem mahā́nt-, not *méǵh₂ (whose exact Vedic match is máhi), so an exact credit for it would be a false positive, and ἠέλιος is a derivative of the sun word: both members are formation-level in at least one branch. Gk ἠέλιος has no key in the builder's reflex table.

path: erratum:sū́rya- 'sun' mapped as the heteroclite *sóh₂wl̥ itself

notes: Helios is θεῶν σκοπὸν ἠδὲ καὶ ἀνδρῶν 'watcher of gods and men' (Hymn. Dem. 62, checked in GLAUx 0013-002: Ἠέλιον … θεῶν σκοπὸν, both acc. sg., σκοπόν tagged APOS); Sūrya is spáśaṃ víśvasya jágataḥ 'spy of all that moves' (RV 4.13.3, checked). Ved. spáś- = *spéḱs; Gk σκοπός is an o-grade thematic derivative of the same root, so the head is shared at root level only (not 'Kuhn's equation'). Copula removed: the daughters have apposition at RV 4.13.3 (táṃ sū́ryaṃ ... spáśam, objects of vahanti) and Hymn. Hom. Dem. 62 (Ἠέλιον ... σκοπόν), so the line is a noun phrase with the watcher in apposition to the Sun. Revised: the genitives 'of gods and men' were dropped: they have no counterpart in RV 4.13.3, and h₂nḗr had been verified through the compound nr̥cákṣas- of another hymn (RV 7.60.2). Case: accusative, as in both parallels (r4: the np had defaulted to NOM): RV 4.13.3 tám sū́ryam … spáśam (VedaWeb ACC SG, objects of vahanti) and Hymn. Dem. 62 Ἠέλιον … σκοπόν (object of ἵκοντο). Formation (r4): Ved. sū́rya- is a -ya- derivative and ἠέλιος another derivative of the sun word, so *sóh₂wl̥ is formation-level in both (an exact credit for sū́rya- would be a false positive). The genitives of what is watched (víśvasya jágataḥ / θεῶν … ἀνδρῶν) are not cognate and stay out.

notes: The Sun's wheel: Ved. cakrám of Sūrya (eleven times; RV 2.11.20 'as Sūrya sets his wheel rolling', ávartayat), Greek ἡλίου κύκλος (Aesch. Pers. 504 etc.; Eur. El. 464f., cited from West 2007 ch. 5), and in the Edda the elves call the sun fagrahvél 'fair wheel' (Alvíssmál 16, beside sól and sunna). All three continue *kʷékʷlos and *sóh₂wl̥ (Gk ἥλιος from *seh₂wel-iyos). Interpolated: the causative wortéye- 'turn' (Ved. vartáya-, Vedic only in these passages); present for the habitual.

notes: Ved. mahó ájmasya 'the great drive' (RV 4.53.4, of Savitr̥'s course, checked) = Gk μέγας ὄγμος (Hymn. Hom. 32.11, the Moon's orbit; not in local corpora); West 2007 ch. 5 calls it an exact equivalent (cf. Watkins 1995: 16). Ved. ájma- (*h₂éǵ-mn̥) and Gk ὄγμος (*h₂óǵ-mos) are different formations of one root, so the head is root-level. Interpolated: the verb h₂eǵ- 'drive' (the root of both nouns; the Vedic has rājati 'rules over' with the genitive) and the locative. Revised: the subject 'the Sun' (Vedic Savitr̥, Greek the Moon) was interpolated and is dropped (3rd sg. pro-drop).
